transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-18 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Singh (NimbleHealth), Owen Hart (Platform Lead), Lina Park (Security)
Links shared: https://redwood.internal/decks/rdw-model-benchmarks.pdf, https://redwood.internal/security/soc2-hipaa.zip

Summary: quick discovery focused on model choices (open models), required context length for clinical notes, multilingual support for triage channels, and tool-calling for EHR lookups. Security questions around PHI/HIPAA, VPC/private deployment, KMS and audit logs.

Transcript: 
[00:00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone thanks for making time, uh this is Maya from Redwood, with Rafael on the call who is our systems engineer, we'll do a quick intro then dive into models and ops constraints, is that ok?
[00:00:10] Priya: yes thanks, im Priya, head of ml at nimblehealth, we've been evaluating open models for triage and note summarization, we're curious about hosting vs dedicated vs private given PHI and latency needs.
[00:00:20] Owen: quick thing from infra side, we need to understand VPC options, key management, and if there's any air-gapped onprem possibility for the POC.
[00:00:28] Rafael (SE): totally, we'll cover the differences. short version, hosted is fastest to get started, dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity, private gives VPC/onprem with customer-managed KMS and audit logs. For HIPAA folks we typically recommend private or dedicated with strict network controls.
[00:00:45] Lina (Security): can you clarify what data flows out of our network in hosted mode? we have to track egress of PHI.
[00:00:52] Maya: yes hosted means requests hit our hosted control plane, we offer encryption in transit and at rest, but for PHI we often see customers choose dedicated with a private network peering or private where the control plane sits in your VPC. we'll share the SOC2 and HIPAA notes after.
[00:01:05] Priya: great — model side, our main tasks: 1) triage classification from referral text, 2) summarization and extraction from long clinical notes up to 16k tokens, sometimes more. also need Spanish and Portuguese for some call centers.
[00:01:20] Rafael: ok so context length is key. we support variants across models and we have runtime support for 8k/32k/64k context windows depending on model and quantization. practical question: do you need full 64k or can you do sliding window + retrieval?
[00:01:35] Priya: for some summaries we need roughly 12–18k, for others, yes a retrieval layer that pulls in chunks is OK. but the triage models need to see entire referral which is usually short.
[00:01:50] Owen: latency constraints — our SLAs for triage are in the 300–600ms range p95. is that achievable?
[00:01:58] Rafael: depends on model size and batch profiles. small 7–13B models running on dedicated pools at optimized batching can hit sub-500ms p95 for single-shot classification. For 32k summaries you'll see higher latencies, but caching and prefix KV cache helps. we can approximate using our benchmark sheet.
[00:02:15] Priya: ok we've been testing Llama variants and a couple of Mistral forks, curious about quality delta vs cost. do you have perf numbers?
[00:02:23] Maya: sent a link to model benchmarks in the chat, it's the deck we shared. rafael, can you summarize tradeoffs?
[00:02:28] Rafael: sure. broadly: Mistral/falcon family do well cost-wise with good multi-turn; Llama-2 and derivatives often better for instruction tuning and extraction but need more compute or quantization. memory and kv cache behavior differs — some models are more friendly to 4-bit quant and keep quality. we recommend running a small eval on your prompts.
[00:02:45] Owen: question about tool-calling — we need secure EHR lookup integrations and the ability to call internal APIs for patient verification. is function/tool calling supported and can we keep requests inside VPC?
[00:02:56] Rafael: yes we support tool-calling and function-like calls. with private deployments the tool execution can be run inside your network so payloads never leave. with hosted, you'd need connector tunnels or a secure webhook pattern. there are options for signed webhooks and on-prem agents.
[00:03:12] Lina: for audit we need immutable logs of who called what, with token-level tracing. is that available?
[00:03:17] Maya: yes our console provides per-request traces, token-level cost breakdowns, and you can export audit logs to your SIEM. for private we can integrate with your SIEM via syslog or cloud logging.
[00:03:26] Priya: what about PII scrubbing or post-processing — can we keep raw prompts out of logs?
[00:03:31] Rafael: yes retention and redaction policies are configurable; hosted defaults to masked logs for sensitive customers and dedicated/private can be set to no retention. we'll share configuration docs.
[00:03:40] Priya: good. another concern: multilingual quality — Spanish and Portuguese must be at least 90% accuracy for entity extraction. any references or prior customers?
[00:03:49] Maya: we have a couple of healthcare customers running multilingual pipelines; we can share anonymized evals. also recommend a two-step approach: classification in the original language then canonicalization in English if that helps.
[00:04:02] Owen: for the pilot we want to compare three model configs: a cost-optimized 13B quantized on dedicated, a 30–40B on dedicated for higher quality, and a private deployment using 70B with 32k context. can the Redwood runtime host all three and route based on policy?
[00:04:16] Rafael: yes that's exactly what routing policies do — region, latency, or cost-based routing, plus automatic fallback to smaller variants if capacity's limited. we can orchestrate canary rollouts and A/B.
[00:04:28] Priya: wonderful. budget question — if we run a 4-week pilot with 10k calls/day, what's typical monthly cost range for dedicated vs hosted?
[00:04:36] Maya: i'll send sims in the benchmark sheet but rough back-of-envelope: cost per token and reserved GPU hours drive it. dedicated gives lower per-token for sustained load but has minimums. hosted is pay-as-you-go and easier to start. i'll include numbers.
[00:04:50] Priya: any blockers on HIPAA?
[00:04:53] Lina: specifically need BAAs, encryption with customer-managed KMS, audit trails, and data residency in us-east for the POC.
[00:04:59] Maya: we do BAA for Private and Dedicated enterprise tiers; KMS integrations supported, and we can pin region to us-east. we'll attach the legal and compliance packet.
[00:05:10] Owen: when can we get a POC? we're aiming to start on Aug 30.
[00:05:14] Rafael: SE time ok — we can provision a dedicated pool and a private eval cluster, maybe need 3–4 business days for private VPC setup once we have network contacts.
[00:05:24] Priya: checklist — we need: 1) benchmark/latency sims, 2) pilot acceptance criteria and test prompts, 3) SOC2/HIPAA docs, 4) list of required network contacts.
[00:05:34] Maya: noted, we'll send all three items. next steps and owners we'll capture in the follow-up email.
[00:05:40] Owen: small nit — for the 32k and 64k contexts does Redwood support efficient sliding windows or streaming to reduce memory?
[00:05:47] Rafael: yes we have streaming and sliding window helpers in runtime, plus KV cache to reduce recomputation. for long docs we often combine retrieval + streaming with chunk overlap.
[00:05:58] Priya: okay last thing: can we run a quick toy test this week with a sanitized sample? if we get results we'll fast-track the POC.
[00:06:04] Maya: absolutely, Rafael will own that.
[00:06:06] Rafael: yes I'll set up a small hosted eval with a sanitized sample and run it against the three model configs, share results in the sheet.
[00:06:13] Lina: thanks everyone, appreciate the responsiveness.
[00:06:16] Maya: thanks all, i'll follow up with the deck, cost sims and SOC2 link and propose an Aug 30 kickoff for the pilot; Rafael will send the toy-run results by end of week.
[00:06:27] Priya: sounds good.
[00:06:30] -- end of meeting --

Action recap (verbatim):
- Maya Chen to send benchmark spreadsheet and hosted vs dedicated cost sims by 2027-08-20.
- Rafael Ortiz to draft POC acceptance criteria and run toy test on sanitized sample, share results in sheet by 2027-08-20.
- Owen Hart to confirm stakeholders and provisioning window by 2027-08-22.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings for technical terms (k v cache transcribed as queue cache in one segment), speaker overlap around 00:02:28–00:02:45. overall medium quality.
